title: Adopt Pi as the agent harness and its session schema as the Chatticus transcript
description:
Direction from the human (2026-10-04): integrate the Pi coding agent harness deeply. Chatticus has no real session storage format, so adopt Pi's session format (tree of entries with id/parentId) and Pi's detailed message schema as the canonical transcript; every Chatticus message revolves around that schema. Pi streams events; Chatticus becomes the user interface for Pi, streaming its responses into the existing one-turn stream.

First step: research Pi's session/message/event schema and embedding APIs from source, then a design note mapping it onto Chatticus constraints (DynamoDB as the transcript store, channels with several bots, one-turn streams with no sockets, the computer vs Lambda split, approvals) and a migration of existing messages (no dual readers).

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Research (2026-10-04, earendil-works/pi @ 2003871, packages 1.0.2, MIT; @mariozechner/* deprecated): session format v3 = header + entry tree (id/parentId) of message, model_change, thinking_level_change, usage, compaction, branch_summary, custom, custom_message, context_edit, label, session_info; system prompt and tools live in the transcript as system messages. Messages: user (no author field), assistant (text/thinking/toolCall blocks, usage+cost, stopReason, errorMessage), toolResult. SessionManager.inMemory(cwd, opts, entries) lets a host own storage -> one DynamoDB item per entry. Events: agent/turn/message start-update-end with text/thinking/toolcall deltas, tool_execution_*, agent_settled; RPC wire is delta-only. tool_call hook is awaited and can block (approvals). Bash/read/write/edit take pluggable operations -> Pi can run outside the computer while its tools execute on it. Node >= 22.19, ESM; Lambda viability unverified. pi-durable has a pluggable Storage interface but is experimental.

DECISION (human, 2026-10-04): one Pi session per bot per channel. A bot's own turns are native Pi messages; human and other-bot channel messages are injected as custom_message entries with attribution in the content.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Storage decision (human, 2026-10-04): Pi sessions are stored in DynamoDB, not JSONL files on EFS. One item per Pi session entry (session key = tenant + channel + bot; sort by append order; the item holds the entry verbatim: id, parentId, type, payload), so Pi's format is preserved and a .jsonl export is one line per item. Lambdas stay out of any VPC (no NAT, no IPv6 dependency); matches 'the transcript is DynamoDB' and zero idle cost. The worker loads entries into SessionManager.inMemory(...) per turn and writes back the entries Pi appended (diff, since entry_appended does not fire for ordinary messages), with conditional writes on the turn fence. Entries over the 400 KB item limit offload to S3 with a pointer. pi-durable's Storage interface is the likely long-term backend once it is stable.

comments.author: home
comments.text: DECISION (human, 2026-10-04, after earendil.com/posts/pi-durable): build on pi-durable as the engine, not the coding agent's session layer. pi-durable gives durable tasks with checkpoints and crash resume, idempotent requestId submissions, documents committed atomically with the transcript, multiple humans steering the same agents, and a pluggable Storage interface with a conformance suite. Target mapping: a DynamoDB Storage backend; one storage per bot conversation (bot x channel); the turn Lambda becomes that storage's single owner for the turn under the existing fence lease, resumes unfinished tasks, commits, exits; per-turn SSE stream fed from watchEvents() (no sockets). If it holds, pi-durable's durability replaces Chatticus's turn/attempt/lease/recovery machinery and its entries become the transcript. Accepted risk: experimental API.

right_now_summary: The team is testing the DynamoDB turn flow, including recovery, tools, and Lambda cold starts.
